messages:
incidentbot: PagerDuty escalation fired for service=hosted-inference, urgency=high. Primary acked, secondary did NOT ack within 2m -> manager notified. PagerDuty incident: INC-5001. Trigger: sustained 503 surge in us-west1.
kevin: oncall here, seeing PD alert. jumping in. what’s customer impact?
alex: I’m pulling the dashboard now. 5xx rate spiked from 0.2% -> 18% over last 3m for ws:generate. Latency also increased. Looks localized to us-west1 hosts behind model-variant v1.
maria: confirmed in Console -> per-route traces show KV cache thrash on g4dn pool. Errors are ENOMEM / grpc stream resets. Some requests are retrying -> cascading.
sre_oncall: good context. mitigation idea: 1) remove us-west1 from smart-routing for hosted-inference 2) enable fallback routing to model-quantized-compat 3) scale dedicated pool if needed. can someone flip routing?
alex: I can do 1 and 2. running: 
```bash
# temporarily disable us-west1 routing
redwoodctl routing set --service hosted-inference --exclude-region us-west1 --reason "PD escalation - temporary fallback"
# enable fallback model
redwoodctl routing set --service hosted-inference --fallback-model model-quantized-compat
```
output: routing updated, fallback enabled.
maria: added a note in incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/INCIDENTS/INC-5001. tagging customers with >1% error: acme-corp, paymentflow.
emily: customer-impact: acme-corp reports degraded checkouts (errors ~12% of their requests), paymentflow sees elevated latency but retries masked it. notifying support to open proactive outbound to top customers.
oncall-rotation: manager notified by PD. ETA for manager ack was 4m, they’re awake and joining if needed.
kevin: alex thanks — are we seeing error rate drop after reroute?
alex: early signal: total 5xx down from 18% -> 4% in 90s. some hosts still flapping.
sre_oncall: can we scale pool as well? do a cautious +2 to g4dn pool, hold for 2m and watch.
amendment from alex (command): 
```bash
# scale up inference deployment replicas
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/hosted-inference-g4dn --replicas=12
```
output: scaled, new pods provisioning.
maria: I'm seeing new pods healthy, readiness passing. KV cache warm-up will take a minute; we should keep fallback enabled for at least 10m.
emily: support notified acme-corp via ticket #SUP-2123, provided status + ETA. assigned SRE contacts.
kevin: opening incident bridge (meet link dropped): https://meet.redwood.com/bridge/INC-5001 :flag-us: please join if you’re coordinating.
oncall-rotation: manager here — thanks. please keep PD notes updated and mark any customer-facing actions. If secondary remains unresponsive we'll update escalation policy to avoid manager fatigue.
sre_oncall: monitoring: backend 503s back to 0.6% after 4m. latency  p95 from 1.2s -> 900ms. rolling error is trending down.
alex: removing exclude-region us-west1 deferred until stable. leaving fallback-model enabled for 12m then evaluate.
maria: posted short postmortem template in incident doc. initial impact: 7 regions affected indirectly by retries, primary customer exposure: acme-corp (~2k failed requests), paymentflow degraded. estimated customer minutes impacted ~18k.
emily: support will send proactive emails in next 10m, CS on standby for calls.
kevin: next steps: 1) keep bridge open for loopbacks 2) watch for PD re-escalations 3) add follow-up runbook items to prevent KV cache thrash (limiting simultaneous cold starts). assigning alex to mitigation follow-up, maria to customer comms.
incidentbot: PagerDuty note added: responder=kevin, status=acknowledged, escalation=manager-alerted.
sre_oncall: thanks all. marking this thread for a post-incident follow-up. if error rate holds low for 15m we can close PD and bridge.
alex: error rate stable ~0.4% for 10m now. I'll keep an eye and start a short timeline in the doc.
maria: final check — no new 504/503 in logs for top 10 customers. support confirmed outbound for acme-corp done.
oncall-rotation: will close PD after 20m stable. good job everyone. :thumbsup:
